newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may start PBI sale talks next week.
newsitem.headline: Poland may start PBI sale talks next week.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland (NBP) may start talks with prospective investors bidding for a strategic stake in Polish Investment Bank SA (PBI) next week, the central bank's spokeswoman said on Monday.
"On Friday the NBP board will initially aquaint itself with the (PBI) offers and perhaps next week there will be talks with potential investors," Renata Winiewska told Reuters.
Late in January the Nowa Europa business daily said that two foreign investors and one domestic investor remained in the bidding for PBI shares, including GE Capital and Creditanstalt.
PBI, which was recently awarded a BBB- long-term rating by IBCA, made a net profit of 54.9 million zlotys last year, up from 26.2 million zlotys in 1995.
The medium-sized Polish bank was carved out of the NBP in 1993 with a clean credit portfolio and is 100- percent owned by the central bank, which wants to substantially reduce its stake on PBI.
